validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE/CLASSIFICATION: real, well-documented, correctly-classified Texas intrastate natural gas transmission line. Independently confirmed across at least five origins spanning construction through 2023: World Pipelines (trade press, 2014-11-18, 'NET completes construction of Mexico Pipeline'), Natural Gas Intelligence (2014-11-17, 'NET Mexico Pipeline Officially Online Ahead of Schedule'), offshore-technology.com/hydrocarbons-technology.com (project profile, published Jan 2015), PR Newswire (NextEra's own 2015 acquisition release and its 2013 presidential-permit release), a second NGI article (2017, Los Ramones II context), and 2023 trade coverage of the Kinder Morgan sale (Natural Gas Intelligence, East Daley Analytics via eastdaley.com). Not a GEM-only entity by any measure. DUPLICATE CHECK against the 45-row TX-operating roster: no other row matches this physical pipe (Valley Crossing/P0276, Sur de Texas-Tuxpan/P0257, and Agua Blanca/P2499 all touch the same Agua Dulce corridor but are distinct, separately-owned lines with different capacities/owners) -- no duplicate flag. SPEC CONFIRMATIONS: Length 124 mi (200 km) matches hydrocarbons-technology exactly; World Pipelines' 2014 article separately states '120 mile' -- a ~3% variance, below the material-conflict threshold, likely a pre-final-tally vs as-built figure, so treated as a caveat not a conflict. Diameter 42in confirmed by hydrocarbons-technology and World Pipelines; note World Pipelines also mentions a 48in segment, but hydrocarbons-technology clarifies that 48in stretch (~1,247 ft) is on the MEXICAN side of the border and is owned/operated by Los Ramones (a separate entity/pipeline), not part of this US-side GEM row -- so Diameter=42 (US segment only) is correct as recorded. Capacity 2100 MMcf/d (2.1 Bcf/d) confirmed independently by hydrocarbons-technology, World Pipelines, AND a third source (NGI 2017 Los Ramones article: '2.1 Bcf/d NET Mexico pipeline'). FuelSource 'Agua Dulce Natural Gas Hub' confirmed by hydrocarbons-technology and World Pipelines (both describe the Agua Dulce Hub as the receipt point with 9 interconnecting pipelines / 4bcf/d+ receipt capacity). Location (Nueces County -> Rio Grande City) confirmed by hydrocarbons-technology, the 2017 NGI article ('terminates near Rio Grande, TX'), and 2023 East Daley/NGI coverage ('a border crossing near Rio Grande City, Texas'). Status=operating confirmed continuously: online Nov 2014 (World Pipelines, NGI 2014) through still-flowing 2023 (East Daley: 'flows over the last 30 days have averaged closer to 1.5 Bcf/d', May 2023) and the pipeline was actively being sold as an operating asset in the Dec 2023 Kinder Morgan transaction. ConstructionYear/Month=2014-02: hydrocarbons-technology is the only source giving the specific month ('Construction ... started on February 2014'); the 2014 year and general timeline (FERC presidential permit Nov 2013 -> construction -> mechanical completion Oct 2014 per World Pipelines -> in-service Nov 2014) is corroborated across sources, but the February month specifically is single-sourced -- tier medium, not high, for that one cell. HARVESTED POOL: of this row's 9 wiki-harvested citations, 8 were opened this pass (prnewswire x2, eia.gov, ijglobal x2, hydrocarbons-technology, naturalgasintel/Los Ramones, finance.yahoo.com, eastdaley.com); the 9th (bit.ly/2rWJOGO) resolves to A Barrel Full and was correctly skipped per the standing ban. eia.gov/naturalgas/data.php is a generic data-portal landing page, not an article naming this pipeline -- not usable as a citation for any specific value (navigation-surface problem), though it verifies live. Both ijglobal.com transaction-database links (28108, 36270) now 301/302-redirect through several hops to a generic 'Green Street EU / Infrastructure' marketing page -- the original transaction data is gone (IJGlobal appears to have been absorbed into Green Street); no Wayback snapshot exists for either URL (checked via the CDX availability API). These are dead ends, not deletions of the pipeline itself -- just of that particular paywalled database record -- so not cited.

validity.researcher_notes: STALE OWNERSHIP, found via fresh web search (not in the wiki's harvested citation pool, which predates this event): NextEra Energy Partners (NEP) closed the sale of its entire Texas natural gas pipeline portfolio -- branded 'STX Midstream', of which the NET Mexico pipeline (90% interest) was explicitly the largest asset -- to Kinder Morgan, Inc. on 2023-12-28, for $1.815 billion. Confirmed independently by: (1) NEP's own PR Newswire release, 'NextEra Energy Partners, LP completes sale of Texas natural gas pipeline portfolio' (2023-12-28, states the Kinder Morgan deal closed); (2) Kinder Morgan's own investor-relations release, 'Kinder Morgan to Purchase NextEra Energy Partner's STX Midstream' (2023-11-06), which states verbatim: 'STX Midstream includes a 90% interest in the NET Mexico pipeline; MGI Enterprises, a PEMEX affiliate, owns the other 10%' -- this is a genuine THIRD-PARTY-style cross-check because it is the ACQUIRER's own statement of the target's cap table, not NEP's; (3) independent trade press, Natural Gas Intelligence ('Kinder Morgan Adding Nearly 5 Bcf/d of South Texas Natural Gas Capacity in $1.8B Deal With NextEra') and Pipeline & Gas Journal / pipeline-journal.net, both reporting the same close. Sheet LastUpdated=2023-08-28 predates both the Nov 2023 announcement and the Dec 2023 close, so NextEra Energy was correct as of that update but the row has not been revisited since -- this is a straightforward staleness gap, not a research error, and it directly disproves the wiki page's own framing (which still shows NextEra as owner). MGI Enterprises 10% is UNCHANGED and reconfirmed by the same Kinder Morgan release, so no concern on Owner2. Do not auto-apply -- routed to Update per standing rules (never auto-apply a value change).

validity.researcher_notes: GEM records SegmentCost=760,000,000 USD. The one specific-cost figure I could independently verify, hydrocarbons-technology.com (a live, verifier-passing source), states 'The $665m intrastate pipeline project was financed by a consortium of lenders led by the Bank of Tokyo-Mitsubishi UFJ' -- i.e. $665 million, not $760 million, a ~14% disagreement (over the 10% material-conflict threshold). I could not independently corroborate the $760M figure this pass: both IJGlobal transaction-database URLs harvested from the wiki page (which likely originated the $760M figure, going by the wiki's own citation numbering) now redirect to an unrelated Green Street marketing page with no live transaction data and no Wayback snapshot available; a WebSearch-generated summary surfaced a '$760 million project cost' + '$664 million debt financing' split (which would actually be CONSISTENT with hydrocarbons-technology's $665M debt figure if $760M is total project cost vs $665M is just the debt tranche -- these could be two different, non-conflicting numbers: total cost vs. debt financing amount) but I could not trace that composite figure to a live, independently-checkable primary source distinct from GEM's own wiki content, so it is not citable. Net: the $760M/$665M pairing may in fact be two compatible figures (total capex vs. debt-only), which would mean no real conflict -- but I cannot confirm that reading from an independent source, so I'm flagging it as unresolved rather than either confirming or silently keeping it.

fills.researcher_notes: World Pipelines (2014) reports the line 'now operational and able to deliver natural gas to Mexico'; East Daley's 2023 note independently reports it still actively flowing ('flows over the last 30 days have averaged closer to 1.5 Bcf/d') nine years later, and it was sold as an in-service asset in Dec 2023. Continuous operating evidence spanning 2014-2023.
Both sources describe it plainly as a natural gas transmission/intrastate pipeline moving natural gas to Mexico.

Single source states the specific month: 'Construction on the pipeline started on February 2014 and the commissioning activities concluded in October 2014.' The 2014 year and the general sequence (FERC presidential permit Nov 2013 -> construction -> mechanical completion Oct 2014 per World Pipelines) are corroborated elsewhere, but no second source names February specifically, so tier is medium rather than high for this cell.
Three independent trade/industry sources (World Pipelines 2014-11-18, NGI 2014-11-17, hydrocarbons-technology Jan 2015) all place in-service in November 2014, ahead of a scheduled Dec 1, 2014 date.

hydrocarbons-technology: 'initially operates with a capacity of 2.1Bcf/d'; World Pipelines: firm transport agreement 'for up to 2.1 billion ft3/d'; NGI (2017): '2.1 Bcf/d NET Mexico pipeline'. Three independent sources, exact match to GEM's 2100 MMcf/d.

hydrocarbons-technology states '200km-long (124 miles)', an exact match. World Pipelines' 2014 construction-completion article separately says '120 mile' -- a ~3% variance, below the material-conflict bar but enough that I'm not calling this a clean 2-source agreement; tier medium rather than high pending a source that reconciles 120 vs 124.

Both sources cite the mainline as 42in. hydrocarbons-technology clarifies World Pipelines' additional '48 in.' mention belongs to a short (~1,247 ft) Mexican-side segment owned/operated by Los Ramones, a separate entity -- not part of this US-side GEM row -- so 42in alone is correct here.
Both describe the Agua Dulce Hub in Nueces County as the receipt point feeding this pipeline from nine interconnecting pipelines / 4+ Bcf/d of receipt capacity.

hydrocarbons-technology: 'Agua Dulce, Nueces County, Texas' to 'a point near Rio Grande City' in Starr County. NGI 2017 independently: 'terminates near Rio Grande, TX'. East Daley's 2023 note (used as a corroborating third source elsewhere) also says 'a border crossing near Rio Grande City, Texas' -- both endpoints are correctly recorded on the sheet as US-side locations; the pipeline's Mexican continuation is a separate entity (Los Ramones), correctly out of scope for this US GEM row.
